global_silver_linings.title: The ‘Domino Chains’ Transforming Kidney Donation
global_silver_linings.snippet: A guy goes into a bar, and leaves with one less kidney. That’s a joke Mark Scotch tells about his life. It’s only a slight exaggeration: A chance encounter in 2020 did lead to him donating a kidney — although not quite in the way he expected.
global_silver_linings.reason: Domino-chain kidney donation — where one stranger's gift triggers a cascade of matched transplants — is quietly saving lives that the traditional system couldn't reach. Each chain proves that a single act of generosity can multiply far beyond what any one person imagined possible.

discovery_articles.title: Saint Olaf's Church of England in England
discovery_articles.snippet: Deep in the spectacular Lake District National Park sits the tiny hamlet of Wasdale Head, located in the shadow of England's highest mountain, Scafell Pike, and near the shores of England's deepest lake, Wastwater. Within the hamlet, the minute Saint Olaf's Church of England, at just 142 cubic meters, is England's smallest active parish church. Originally equipped with merely a few seats and an earth floor, the church now has enough pew seating to snuggly accommodate a maximum of 39 people.

discovery_articles.title: The Saugerties Lighthouse  in Saugerties, New York
discovery_articles.snippet: At the confluence of the Esopus Creek and the Hudson River in Saugerties, NY you will find the charming Saugerties Lighthouse. Built in 1869 it has guided ships away from the shallows and into the Esopus Creek for 157 years. Today the lighthouse is maintained by the Saugerties Lighthouse Conservancy and functions as a living museum and bed & breakfast.

featured_read.title: Games People Play: The Revolutionary 1964 Model of Human Relationships That Changed How We (Mis)Understand Ourselves and Each Other
featured_read.snippet: "Because there is so little opportunity for intimacy in daily life, and because some forms of intimacy (especially if intense) are psychologically impossible for most people, the bulk of the time in serious social life is taken up with playing games."
featured_read.blurb: Eric Berne's 1964 theory asks an uncomfortable question: what if most of our daily interactions aren't connection at all, but elaborate scripts we run to avoid it? A quiet half-hour with this one might change how you hear your next conversation before it's even finished.
